name: Digest-driven overseer
description: Builds a capped compact digest of the run, makes one structured model call with a fixed prompt and tool schema, validates the answer against the five signals, and returns proceed on any error, non-object response or unknown signal.
advantages: Very low token cost, safe by default, and cannot distort a run without an explicit signal. Selected because: RunnerConfig.overseer
disadvantages: Quality rests on the digest keeping the right evidence and on a model deciding well, and the live signal match is unmeasured.

name: Rebuilt prompt per step with a referenced context (today)
description: Each step is a fresh planner call built from the template, the cached head and context layers, the newest observations in full and older ones in one line; from the second step the transcript and the context block are replaced by a short note that refers to step one.
advantages: Built and selected; the smallest planner input per step; the final answer still sees everything.
disadvantages: From the second step the planner sees neither the transcript nor the context block, and is told it saw them; continuity across steps is unmeasured.

name: Separate stores read at the start of a request (today)
description: Conversation recall, recent context, feedback guidance, predictions, reflections and quest cards are each read separately at the start of a request and prepended to the context block, fenced per quest or global; a representative's learned notes and context preferences are read with no scope; declined proposals arrive from the host's escalation history.
advantages: Built; each store is measured on its own; a failure in one does not stop the others.
disadvantages: No view of what an intent or the quest settled; several budgets and paths, each of which must apply the fence; the representative's notes cross quests; chat and background work read different subsets.

name: Code-enforced before and after on deep runs only (today)
description: Around every deep goal the slice is found, the metric is read before and after by the runner's meters, rows go to the ledger, and a changed run with nothing on record is asked once and otherwise marked missing; chat turns and in-process work are not covered.
advantages: Built and shown in the terminal and the host's chat; decided from the ledger, never from words.
disadvantages: Covers only deep runs; nothing acts on a regression or a missing metric; no metric is proposed when none applies.

name: Rebuilt prompt per step with the context re-sent from cache
description: The same per-step call with the reference note switched off (planner_abbreviate_repeat_context), so every step re-sends the transcript and context block as an unchanged prefix a caching provider reads from cache.
advantages: No new code; every step sees what the first saw; the cached prefix stays identical across steps.
disadvantages: Pays for the context on every step, cheaply only where the provider caches it, which is unmeasured here; a step still sees earlier steps only through their observations.

name: Start-of-run card filter and a recency window (today)
description: Cards are filtered once from the request text at the start of the run; afterwards every observation is admitted, the newest few in full and older ones in one line.
advantages: Built; no model call per step; a short run sees everything it read.
disadvantages: Blind to the goal: a finding that matters can be collapsed and a near miss is admitted like a match; the scope fence is applied per store rather than at one gate.

name: No overseer (configuration off)
description: The overseer switched off, so a run is exactly what the planner and its own checks do, with no watcher and no overseer call.
advantages: No cost or latency; nothing argues with a correct decision.
disadvantages: Nothing catches drift, wasted reads or a needed hand-off in a run nobody watches; never compared with the overseer on the same runs.

name: Work-folder sync
description: Mirrors a work item's state and notes into a local file with runner-managed marked sections, and pushes new human notes back once, preserving human-authored text elsewhere in the file.
advantages: Idempotent, keeps human edits, and uses only the existing client methods.
disadvantages: A single shared file can conflict with hand edits near the markers, and direction rules must be respected by callers.
